g.text: How does Kafka internally works to publish record to the queue

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Consumers use offsets to read messages (kinda acts like pagination token),

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: also helps with reading the message only once, when multiple consumers

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: working within the same consumer group.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Consumers periodically commit that last read offset, incase of outages at consumer side.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Kafka maintains what the latest offset was, when it was read.

g.text: * Each partition is designed a leader replica on 1 of the brokers, it is also responsible for handling read and write operations to the partition.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: * Assignment for reader replica is managed centrally for some cluster controller, which makes sure that all the leader replicas are effectively distributed across the cluster.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: * The followers don't handle client requests, Each follower just passively replicates the data from the leader. Effectively acting like a backup, ready to take over if leader, for some reason, goes down.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
